explanation: Fires inside boilerplate header comments of source files, mostly software license/copyright notices (Apache NOTICE 'file', GPL 'as published', 'version', 'distributed with', BSD 'license that') and similar template comments (ComVisible, viewDidLoad, generated-by). The token itself matters little; the license-header context drives it. Ordinary prose gives near zero.

No clear pattern: strongest on 'E' in 'vitamin E' and 'LH' in endocrine text, but also fires moderately on assorted abbreviation/word-completion tokens in scientific and technical text (antioxidant, SRAM, NFV, 'AS IS', -arid) and random function words in everyday text. Hard to predict beyond 'vitamin E'/hormone abbreviations.

Fires on function/connector words in fixed phrasal or formulaic constructions where the next word is highly predictable: 'referred [to]', 'hereina[fter]', 'highlighting [indicates]', 'In the [coming] weeks', 'INCLUDING, [BUT] NOT LIMITED', 'Such', 'Instead', 'rename x [to]'. Depends on the preceding context setting up a set phrase; the activation is broad and diffuse across genres.

Fires in machine-generated math word problems (DeepMind-mathematics style 'Let ... Suppose ... Solve') and LaTeX math, on tokens that start an equation or the next clause: '=' signs, 'Suppose', the space before a number, variable names. Weaker on sentence punctuation in unrelated text.

Fires on middle subword pieces of long technical/chemical/biomedical words (hep[ar]in, cyclod[extr]in, phency[clid]ine, hydro[chlor]ide, meth[ic]illin, flav[iv]irus), plus a separate set of hits on 'to' in 'used to convert'/'Functions to' and on closing brackets in JSON/XML/code. Mostly a mid-word-fragment detector for rare technical words.

Fires on a non-initial subword fragment that completes an unusual word or proper name, especially foreign/rare surnames and names (Yamas[aki], Tymin[ski], Naj[ib], Mi[key], Sam[mi]) and some uncommon words (ax[on], unamb[igu]ously, kh[ich]di, Dan[az]ol). Common words and word-initial tokens give little.

Fires on purpose/infinitival 'to' coming right after a noun phrase or clause that sets up a goal ('use the code below [to] retrieve', 'complete this form [to] have', 'ask questions [to] improve', 'override this method [to] do'). Weaker on other prepositions ('in', 'on', 'from') attached to a preceding verb phrase.

Fires in auto-generated algebra problems on the '=' or '+' operator (or the space before 0) inside equations such as 'Suppose -p + d - 10 = -6*p'; context is 'Suppose/Solve' equation strings. Weaker and scattered on short question/dialogue tokens ('are you?', 'Is that') and digits in case numbers.

Fires on a token that repeats or nearly repeats an earlier phrase in the same document ('snoring patients' after 'snoring', 'supermarket tomatoes', 'Category:' lines in wiki footers, 'Toronto Pride parade', 'Same as above', duplicate import paths). It is driven by the repetition context, not by the token's identity.

Fires on the period or comma right after an abbreviation, place name, time or number that ends a phrase ('N.J[.]', 'p.m[.]', 'U.S[.]', '30 min[.]', 'Tennessee[,]', '2050[.]'), mostly where a factual clause in news or scientific prose ends. Punctuation after ordinary words fires less.

Fires on the boundary token that closes a document header or caption block: the comment close/newline after an Xcode or PHP file header ('//\n', ' */\n'), 'Circuit' in 'United States Court of Appeals, Ninth Circuit.', reporter citation pieces, and Java exception names ('NoClassDefFoundError:'). Fires on the token that ends structured metadata before the body starts.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word split into several tokens, typically non-English words (French 'v'aste, 'v'endredi, German 'Mitt'woch, Portuguese) and long scientific terms (dors'ol'ateral, 'Sup'pressor, 'trans'locations, hy'pon'atremia, polychlorinated 'bip'henyls). Whole common English words fire little.

Fires on predictable words inside standard software license boilerplate, above all 'even' in 'WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty', also 'except' in 'use this file except in compliance', 'that' in 'permitted provided that', 'part' in 'This file is part of'. Outside license text it is weak and scattered.

Fires on words meaning hidden, concealed or secret: 'hidden'/'Hidden', 'lurking', 'hiding', 'secret', 'buried', 'implicit', 'subtly', 'behind', 'deep down'. The token's meaning of concealment is what matters; related words like 'invisible' or 'shadow' fire moderately.
